answer.summary: Jessica learned to avoid setting goals on hard-to-move long-term outcomes or using complicated composite metrics nobody understands. Instead, use measurable short-term proxies, and don’t let averages hide rare but severe failures.

sections.heading: Metric-setting mistakes to avoid
sections.content: She says retention is a poor short-term goal because it is difficult to move meaningfully and quickly. Rather than goal directly on it, identify short-term inputs that may drive the long-term outcome and test that relationship through experimentation. She also cautions against elaborate weighted composite metrics: they can be hard to understand and interpret—for example, whether a 0.1 change is good or meaningful. She favors simple proxy metrics that teams can measure and understand.

sections.heading: Don’t overlook rare failures
sections.content: Averages can also conceal severe edge cases. DoorDash set goals around “Never Delivered” orders because they were rare but costly and harmful to customers; the aim was to reduce them, not assume average performance told the whole story.
